# Claude Opus 5 via Claude CLI Setup

Use the current Codex session as the main agent and one
persistent Claude CLI session as the sidekick.

## Verify

Use `claude-opus-5` at medium effort for the
persistent sidekick. Retain the current main agent's model and reasoning
effort, and pin the sidekick model and effort explicitly rather than relying
on user configuration.
Include this in every assignment: preserve accurate existing comments.
Keep new comments sparse, concise, and only for non-obvious constraints or
rationale that clear code cannot express. Do not narrate or restate code;
remove redundant new comments before returning.
Verify the CLI once before the first assignment in the current context:

```bash
command claude --version
```

Keep the work in the main agent and report the limitation when Claude is
unavailable, unauthenticated, or rejects the configured model.

## Start

Write the compact assignment to a prompt file using the environment's approved
file-writing mechanism — never inline shell quoting. Set `REPO`,
`PROMPT_FILE`, and `OUT` to absolute paths. Mint a unique UUID as `SESSION_ID`
before the run and record it immediately. Use `command claude` to bypass any
interactive shell wrapper. The commands below default to `--max-turns 80`;
the main agent may change or remove that cap when the assignment warrants it.

Start the sidekick with full repository access except for Claude's `Task` tool,
which enforces the no-delegation boundary:

```bash
SESSION_ID=$(uuidgen | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
(cd "$REPO" \
  && CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS=1 command claude -p \
  --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
  --model claude-opus-5 \
  --effort medium \
  --max-turns 80 \
  --output-format json \
  --permission-mode bypassPermissions --disallowedTools=Task \
  < "$PROMPT_FILE" > "$OUT" 2>/dev/null)
```

Run it in a supervised long-running execution session so the main agent can
continue independent judgment work while Claude executes. Retain the same
`SESSION_ID` across exploration, implementation, testing, and correction while
the sidekick's context remains trustworthy.

## Observe

Wait on the existing supervised execution session until it exits, then inspect
the single-result JSON in `OUT`. Treat its `is_error`, `result`, `session_id`,
and process exit as completion evidence; Claude can report an authentication
or model error in JSON even when the process exits successfully. Confirm that
the returned `session_id` equals the UUID recorded before launch. Apply the
main routing event loop to the session and its result.

## Continue

After a formal return, write an authorized focused follow-up to a new prompt
file and a new `OUT` path, then resume the recorded sidekick:

```bash
(cd "$REPO" \
  && CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS=1 command claude -p \
  --resume "$SESSION_ID" \
  --model claude-opus-5 \
  --effort medium \
  --max-turns 80 \
  --output-format json \
  --permission-mode bypassPermissions --disallowedTools=Task \
  < "$PROMPT_FILE" > "$OUT" 2>/dev/null)
```

Never use bare `--continue` when several Claude sessions may exist. Delete each
prompt file after its invocation completes, and preserve the result JSON until
its evidence is recorded.

## Stop And Recover

When the main routing event loop authorizes a health check or recovery, match
only the sidekick process by its recorded session UUID:

```bash
pgrep -fl -- "$SESSION_ID" || true
```

Interrupt only that process and preserve its result file and useful evidence.
If routing selects replacement, mint one new UUID and start a fresh session
with the same model plus a compact handoff, then disclose that the cached
context was lost.

Invoke `spawn_agent` for each initial formal validation pass with this

